description:
Canonical pattern (crate-jmap-mail-server/src/memory.rs:341-343):

    let obj: O = O::deserialize(val).map_err(|e| {
        MemoryError(format!("deserialize {}: {e}", O::TYPE_NAME))
    })?;

Siblings strip the O::TYPE_NAME context (crate-jmap-calendars-server/src/memory.rs:355, :368, :600, :608, :654; same pattern in chat-server, contacts-server, sharing-server, tasks-server, filenode-server — ~30 sites in total):

    Err(e) => return Err(MemoryError(e.to_string())),
    .map_err(|e| BackendSetError::Other(MemoryError(e.to_string())))

When a deserialize fails in production debugging or in CI test logs, the canonical's error reads 'deserialize Mailbox: missing field id at line ...' — the type that failed is immediately visible. The siblings' error reads 'missing field id at line ...' — the caller has to guess which of the 7+ object types in the backend triggered it, since the error type alone is 'MemoryError' for all of them.

This is idiomatic-rust error-handling territory: the AGENTS.md error-handling rule says 'error variants that wrap String for the message instead of structured fields ... loses the values; a structured variant keeps them accessible to callers who want to handle them.' Strictly speaking even the canonical does primitive-obsession with String — but the canonical at least preserves the contextual key (TYPE_NAME) inside the string, which is the most-useful piece for diagnosis. The siblings drop it.

Why P3 not P2: this is a reference-impl error path (feature-gated 'memory') that callers do not match on; only diagnostic value is lost. Cookie-cutter drift but not a functional bug.

Fix: replace MemoryError(e.to_string()) with MemoryError(format!("deserialize {}: {e}", O::TYPE_NAME)) in the sibling memory.rs files. Mechanical.
title: P3: 5 sibling MemoryBackends discard error context in MemoryError(e.to_string()); canonical mail-server uses MemoryError(format!('deserialize {}: {e}', O::TYPE_NAME))
